paragraphs.sourceText: According to American law, if someone is accused of a crime, he is considered 26 until the court proves the person is guilty.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据美国法律，如果某人被指控犯罪，在法庭证明该人有罪之前，他将被视为无罪。

paragraphs.sourceText: To arrest a person, the police have to be reasonably sure that a crime has been 27 . The police must give the suspect the reasons why they are arresting him and tell him his rights under the law. Then the police take the suspect to the police station, where the name of the person and the 28 against him are formally listed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 要逮捕一个人，警察必须合理确定犯罪行为已经发生。警方必须向嫌疑人提供逮捕他的理由，并告诉他根据法律享有的权利。然后警察将嫌疑人带到警察局，那里会正式列出嫌疑人的姓名和对他的指控。

paragraphs.sourceText: The next step is for the suspect to go before a judge. The judge decides whether the suspect should be kept in jail or 29 . If the suspect has no previous criminal record and the judge feels that he will return to court 30 run away, he can go free. Otherwise, the suspect must put up bail(保释金). At this time, too, the judge will 31 a court lawyer to defend the suspect if he can’t afford one.
paragraphs.translationZh: 下一步是嫌疑人接受法官审判。法官决定是否应将嫌疑人关进监狱或释放。如果嫌疑人没有犯罪记录，并且法官认为他会返回法庭而不是逃跑，那么他可以被释放。否则，嫌疑人必须保释金。此时，如果嫌疑人无力聘请律师，法官也会指定一名法庭律师为嫌疑人辩护。

paragraphs.sourceText: The suspect returns to court a week or two later. A lawyer from the district attorney’s office presents a case against the suspect. The attorney may present 32 as well as witnesses. The judge then decides whether there is enough reason to 33 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 一两周后，嫌疑人返回法庭。地方检察官办公室的一名律师对嫌疑人提出了指控。律师可以出示证据和证人。然后法官决定是否有足够的理由进行审判。

paragraphs.sourceText: The American justice system is very complex and sometimes operates slowly. However, every step is 34 to protect the rights of the people. These individual rights are the 35 of the American government.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国司法系统非常复杂，有时运作缓慢。然而，每一步都是为了保护人民的权利。这些个人权利是美国政府的基础。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 36 to 45 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 36 至 45 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Global warming is a trend toward warmer conditions around the world. Part of the warming is natural; we have experienced a 20,000-year-long warming as the last ice age ended and the ice 36 away. However, we have already reached temperatures that are in 37 with other minimum-ice periods, so continued warming is likely not natural. We are 38 to a predicted worldwide increase in temperatures 39 between 1℃and 6 ℃over the next 100 years. The warming will be more 40 in some areas, less in others, and some places may even cool off. Likewise, the 41 of this warming will be very different depending on where you are—coastal areas must worry about rising sea levels, while Siberia and northern Canada may become more habitable (宜居的) and 42 for humans than these areas are now.

The fact remains, however, that it will likely get warmer, on 43 , everywhere. Scientists are in general agreement that the warmer conditions we have been experiencing are at least in part the result of a human-induced global warming trend. Some scientists 44 that the changes we are seeing fall within the range of random (无规律的）variation—some years are cold, others warm, and we have just had an unremarkable string of warm years 45 —but that is becoming an increasingly rare interpretation in the face of continued and increasing warm conditions.

Directions：In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. The End of the Book?
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一篇附有十个陈述的文章，每个陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题纸上标记相应的字母来回答问题 2. 书的结尾？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Amazon, by far the largest bookseller in the country, reported on May 19 that it is now selling more books in its electronic Kindle format than in the old paper-and-ink format. That is remarkable, considering that the Kindle has only been around for four years. E-books now account for 14 percent of all book sales in this country and are increasing far faster than overall book sales. E-book sales are up 146 percent over last year, while hardback sales increased 6 percent and paperbacks decreased 8 percent.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 迄今为止美国最大的书商亚马逊在 5 月 19 日报道称，目前其电子 Kindle 格式的图书销量超过了旧的纸质和墨水格式的图书。考虑到 Kindle 才问世四年，这已经很了不起了。目前，电子书占该国所有图书销量的 14%，并且增长速度远远快于总体图书销量。电子书销量比去年增长 146%，精装书销量增长 6%，平装书销量下降 8%。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Does this spell the doom of the physical book? Certainly not immediately, and perhaps not at all. What it does mean is that the book business will go through a transformation in the next decade or so more profound than any it has seen since Gutenberg introduced printing from moveable type in the 1450s.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 这是否预示着实体书的灭亡？当然不会立即，也许根本不会。它的真正含义是，图书行业将在未来十年左右经历一场自 1450 年代古腾堡引入活字印刷以来从未有过的深刻变革。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Physical books will surely become much rarer in the marketplace. Mass market paperbacks, which have been declining for years anyway, will probably disappear, as will hardbacks for mysteries, thrillers, “romance fiction,” etc. Such books, which only rarely end up in permanent collections, either private or public, will probably only be available as e-books within a few years. Hardback and trade paperbacks for “serious” nonfiction and fiction will surely last longer. Perhaps it will become the mark of an author to reckon with that he or she is still published in hard copy.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 实体书在市场上肯定会变得更加稀有。多年来一直在下滑的大众市场平装本很可能会消失，悬疑小说、惊悚小说、“浪漫小说”等精装本也将消失。这类书籍很少会被私人或公共永久收藏，几年内可能只会以电子书的形式出现。精装本和平装本换成“严肃”的非小说类和小说类书籍肯定会持续更长时间。或许，他或她仍然以硬拷贝形式出版，这将成为作者不可忽视的标志。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) As for children’s books, who knows? Children’s books are like dog food in that the purchasers are not the consumers, so the market (and the marketing) is inherently strange.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 至于儿童读物，谁知道呢？儿童读物就像狗粮，因为购买者不是消费者，因此市场（和营销）本质上是奇怪的。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) For clues to the book’s future, let’s look at some examples of technological change and see what happened to the old technology.
paragraphs.translationZh: E）为了了解本书未来的线索，让我们看一些技术变革的例子，看看旧技术发生了什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) One technology replaces another only because the new technology is better, cheaper, or both. The greater the difference, the sooner and more thoroughly the new technology replaces the old. Printing with moveable type on paper dramatically reduced the cost of producing a book compared with the old-fashioned ones handwritten on vellum, which comes from sheepskin. A Bible—to be sure, a long book—required vellum made from 300 sheepskins and countless man-hours of labor. Before printing arrived, a Bible cost more than a middle-class house. There were perhaps 50,000 books in all of Europe in 1450. By 1500 there were 10 million.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 一种技术取代另一种技术只是因为新技术更好、更便宜或两者兼而有之。差异越大，新技术取代旧技术的速度就越快、越彻底。与在羊皮制成的牛皮纸上手写的老式书籍相比，在纸上使用活字印刷大大降低了书籍的制作成本。一本《圣经》——确实是一本很长的书——需要用 300 张羊皮和无数工时制成的牛皮纸。在印刷术出现之前，一本《圣经》的价格比一套中产阶级的房子还贵。 1450 年，整个欧洲大约有 50,000 本书。到 1500 年，这一数字已达到 1,000 万本书。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) But while printing quickly caused the handwritten book to die out, handwriting lingered on (继续存在)well into the 16th century. Very special books are still occasionally produced on vellum, but they are one-of-a-kind show pieces.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 但是，虽然印刷术很快导致了手写书籍的消亡，但手写体一直持续到 16 世纪。非常特别的书籍仍然偶尔会在牛皮纸上制作，但它们是独一无二的展示品。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Sometimes a new technology doesn’t drive the old one out, but only parts of it while forcing the rest to evolve. The movies were widely predicted to drive live theater out of the marketplace, but they didn’t, because theater turned out to have qualities movies could not reproduce. Equally, TV was supposed to replace movies but, again, did not.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 有时，一项新技术并不能取代旧技术，而只能取代旧技术的一部分，同时迫使其余技术不断发展。人们普遍预测这些电影将把现场戏剧赶出市场，但事实并非如此，因为事实证明戏剧具有电影无法复制的品质。同样，电视本来应该取代电影，但同样没有。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Movies did, however, fatally impact some parts of live theater. And while TV didn’t kill movies, it did kill second-rate pictures, shorts, and cartoons.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 然而，电影确实对现场戏剧的某些部分产生了致命的影响。虽然电视没有杀死电影，但它确实杀死了二流电影、短片和动画片。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Nor did TV kill radio. Comedy and drama shows (“Jack Benny, “Amos and Andy, “The Shadow”) all migrated to television. But because you can’t drive a car and watch television at the same time, rush hour became radio’s prime time, while music, talk, and news radio greatly enlarged their audiences. Radio is today a very different business than in the late 1940s and a much larger one.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 电视也没有消灭广播。喜剧和戏剧节目（《杰克·本尼》、《阿莫斯和安迪》、《影子》）都转移到了电视上。但由于你不能一边开车一边看电视，高峰时段成为广播的黄金时段，而音乐、谈话和新闻广播则大大扩大了听众。如今的广播行业与 20 世纪 40 年代末期截然不同，而且规模也更大。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Sometimes old technology lingers for centuries because of its symbolic power. Mounted cavalry ( 骑兵)replaced the chariot(二轮战车）on the battlefield around 1000 BC. But chariots maintained their place in parades and triumphs right up until the end of the Roman Empire 1,500 years later. The sword hasn’t had a military function for a hundred years, but is still part of an officer’s full- dress uniform, precisely because a sword always symbolized “ an officer and a gentleman.’’
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 有时，旧技术因其象征力量而存在几个世纪。公元前1000年左右，骑兵在战场上取代了二轮战车。但战车在阅兵和凯旋中的地位一直保持到1500年后罗马帝国的灭亡。剑已经一百年没有军事功能了，但仍然是军官礼服的一部分，正是因为剑一直象征着“军官和绅士”。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Sometimes new technology is a little cranky(不稳定的）at first. Television repairman was a common occupation in the 1950s, for instance. And so the old technology remains as a backup. Steamships captured the North Atlantic passenger business from sail in the 1840s because of its much greater speed. But steamships didn’t lose their sails until the 1880s, because early marine engines had a nasty habit of breaking down. Until ships became large enough (and engines small enough) to mount two engines side by side, they needed to keep sails. (The high cost of steam and the lesser need for speed kept the majority of the world’s ocean freight moving by sail until the early years of the 20th century.)
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 有时，新技术一开始会有点暴躁。例如，电视修理工是 20 世纪 50 年代的常见职业。因此旧技术仍然作为后备。轮船在 1840 年代因其速度快得多而从航行中夺取了北大西洋客运业务。但轮船直到 1880 年代才失去帆，因为早期的船用发动机有坏掉的习惯。直到船舶变得足够大（并且发动机足够小）为了并排安装两台发动机，它们需要保持航行（直到 20 世纪初期，蒸汽成本高且对速度的需求较小，使得世界上大部分海运都通过航行进行。）

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Then there is the fireplace. Central heating was present in every upper- and middle-class home by the second half of the 19th century. But functioning fireplaces remain to this day a powerful selling point in a house or apartment. I suspect the reason is a deep-rooted love of fire. Fire was one of the earliest major technological advances for humankind, providing heat, protection, and cooked food (which is much easier to eat and digest). Human control of fire goes back far enough (over a million years) that evolution could have produced a genetic leaning towards fire as a central aspect of human life.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 然后是壁炉。到 19 世纪下半叶，每个上层和中产阶级家庭都配备了中央供暖系统。但时至今日，功能齐全的壁炉仍然是房屋或公寓的一个强大卖点。我怀疑原因是对火根深蒂固的热爱。火是人类最早的重大技术进步之一，提供热量、保护和熟食（更容易食用和消化）。人类对火的控制可以追溯到很久以前（超过一百万年），进化可能产生了一种倾向于将火作为人类生活核心方面的基因。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Books—especially books the average person could afford—haven’t been around long enough to produce evolutionary change in humans. But they have a powerful hold on many people nonetheless, a hold extending far beyond their literary content. At their best, they are works of art and there is a tactile (触觉的）pleasure in books necessarily lost in e-book versions. The ability to quickly thumb through pages is also lost. And a room with books in it induces, at least in some, a feeling not dissimilar to that of a fire in the fireplace on a cold winter’s night.
paragraphs.translationZh: N）书籍——尤其是普通人能买得起的书籍——存在的时间还不够长，不足以给人类带来进化上的改变。但它们仍然对许多人产生了强大的影响力，其影响力远远超出了其文学内容。在最好的情况下，它们是艺术品，而电子书版本中必然会丢失书籍的触觉乐趣。快速翻阅页面的能力也消失了。至少在某些人看来，一个装满书籍的房间会产生一种与寒冷冬夜壁炉中生火的感觉没有什么不同的感觉。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) For these reasons I think physical books will have a longer existence as a commercial product than some currently predict. Like swords, books have symbolic power. Like fireplaces, they induce a sense of comfort and warmth. And, perhaps, similar to sails, they make a useful backup for when the lights go out.
paragraphs.translationZh: O）出于这些原因，我认为实体书作为商业产品的存在时间将比一些人目前预测的更长。就像剑一样，书籍也具有象征力量。就像壁炉一样，它们会带来舒适和温暖的感觉。也许，与帆类似，它们可以在灯光熄灭时提供有用的备份。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Authors still published in printed versions will be considered important ones.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 仍然以印刷版出版的作者将被视为重要的作者。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Some people are still in favor of printed books because of the sense of touch they can provide.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 有些人仍然喜欢印刷书籍，因为它们可以提供触觉。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. The radio business has changed greatly and now attracts more listeners.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 广播业务发生了很大变化，现在吸引了更多的听众。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49.Contrary to many peopled prediction of its death, the film industry survived.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49.与许多人对电影业消亡的预测相反，电影业幸存了下来。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Remarkable changes have taken place in the book business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 图书业发生了显着变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Old technology sometimes continues to exist because of its reliability.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 旧技术有时因其可靠性而继续存在。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. The increase of e-book sales will force the book business to make changes not seen for centuries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 电子书销量的增长将迫使图书行业做出几个世纪以来未曾见过的改变。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. A new technology is unlikely to take the place of an old one without a clear advantage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 如果没有明显的优势，新技术不可能取代旧技术。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. Paperbacks of popular literature are more likely to be replaced by e-books.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 通俗文学的平装本更有可能被电子书取代。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. A house with a fireplace has a stronger appeal to buyers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 带壁炉的房子对买家来说更具吸引力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions：There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有2个段落。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The question of whether our government should promote science and technology or the liberal arts in higher education isn’t an either/or proposition (命题), although the current emphasis on preparing young Americans for STEM (science, technology, engineering, maths)-related fields can make it seem that way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们的政府是否应该在高等教育中促进科学技术或文科的问题并不是一个非此即彼的命题，尽管目前强调让美国年轻人进入 STEM（科学、技术、工程、数学）相关领域的准备可能看起来是这样。

paragraphs.sourceText: The latest congressional report acknowledges the critical importance of technical training, but also asserts that the study of the humanities (人文学科）and social sciences must remain central components of America’s educational system at all levels. Both areas are critical to producing citizens who can participate effectively in our democratic society, become innovative(创新的）leaders, and benefit from the spiritual enrichment that the reflection on the great ideas of mankind over time provides.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最新的国会报告承认技术培训的至关重要性，但也断言人文学科和社会科学的研究必须仍然是美国各级教育体系的核心组成部分。这两个领域对于培养能够有效参与我们民主社会的公民至关重要，成为创新的领导者，并从对人类伟大思想的反思所带来的精神丰富中受益。

paragraphs.sourceText: Parents and students who have invested heavily in higher education worry about graduates, job prospects as technological advances and changes in domestic and global markets transform professions in ways that reduce wages and cut jobs. Under these circumstances, it’s natural to look for what may appear to be the most “practical” way out of the problem: “Major in a subject designed to get you a job” seems the obvious answer to some, though this ignores the fact that many disciplines in the humanities characterized as “soft” often, in fact, lead to employment and success in the long run. Indeed, according to surveys, employers have expressed a preference for students who have received a broadly-based education that has taught them to write well, think critically, research creatively, and communicate easily.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在高等教育上投入巨资的家长和学生担心毕业生和就业前景，因为技术进步以及国内和全球市场的变化以降低工资和裁员的方式改变了职业。在这种情况下，寻找看似最“实际”的解决问题的方法是很自然的：“主修一门旨在让你找到工作的学科”似乎对某些人来说是显而易见的答案，尽管这忽略了一个事实，即人文学科中的许多学科实际上往往会带来就业和成功。事实上，根据调查，雇主表示更喜欢接受过基础广泛教育的学生，这些教育教会他们良好的写作、批判性思考、创造性的研究和轻松的沟通。

paragraphs.sourceText: Moreover, students should be prepared not just for their first job, but for their 4th and 5th jobs, as there’s little reason to doubt that people entering the workforce today will be called upon to play many different roles over the course of their careers. The ones who will do the best in this new environment will be those whose educations have prepared them to be flexible. The ability to draw upon every available tool and insight—picked up from science, arts, and technology—to solve the problems of the future, and take advantage of the opportunities that present themselves, will be helpful to them and the United States.
paragraphs.translationZh: 此外，学生不仅应该为他们的第一份工作做好准备，还应该为他们的第四份和第五份工作做好准备，因为毫无疑问，今天进入劳动力市场的人们将在其职业生涯中扮演许多不同的角色。在这个新环境中表现最好的人将是那些接受过教育、具备灵活性的人。能够利用从科学、艺术和技术中汲取的一切可用工具和见解来解决未来的问题，并利用出现的机会，将对他们和美国都有帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Energy independence. It has a nice ring to it, doesn’t it? If you think so, you’re not alone, because energy independence has been the dream of American presidents for decades, and never more so than in the past few years, when the most recent oil price shock has been partly responsible for kicking off the great recession.
paragraphs.translationZh: 能源独立。它听起来很漂亮，不是吗？如果您这么认为，那么您并不孤单，因为几十年来，能源独立一直是美国总统的梦想，而且在过去几年中尤其如此，最近的油价冲击是引发经济大衰退的部分原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Energy independence” and its rhetorical(修辞的）companion “energy security” are, however, slippery concepts that are rarely thought through. What is it we want independence from, exactly?
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，“能源独立”及其修辞上的“能源安全”都是很少被深思熟虑的模糊概念。我们到底想要独立于什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: Most people would probably say that they want to be independent from imported oil. But there are reasons that we buy all that oil from elsewhere.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数人可能会说他们希望独立于进口石油。但我们从其他地方购买所有石油是有原因的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The first reason is that we need it to keep our economy running. Yes, there is a trickle(涓涓细流）of biofuel（生物燃料） available, and more may become available, but most biofuels cause economic waste and environmental destruction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第一个原因是我们需要它来保持经济运行。是的，存在着涓涓细流的生物燃料，而且可能还会有更多，但大多数生物燃料会造成经济浪费和环境破坏。

paragraphs.sourceText: Second, Americans have basically decided that they don’t really want to produce all their own oil. They value the environmental quality they preserve over their oil imports from abroad. Vast areas of the United States are off-limits to oil exploration and production in the name of environmental protection. To what extent are Americans really willing to endure the environmental impacts of domestic energy production in order to cut back imports?
paragraphs.translationZh: 其次，美国人基本上已经决定他们并不真的想自己生产所有石油。与从国外进口石油相比，他们更看重自己所保护的环境质量。以环境保护为名，美国大片地区禁止石油勘探和生产。美国人在多大程度上真正愿意忍受国内能源生产对环境的影响以减少进口？

paragraphs.sourceText: Third, there are benefits to trade. It allows for economic efficiency, and when we buy things from places that have lower production costs than we do, we benefit. And although you don’t read about this much, the United States is also a large exporter of oil products, selling about 2 million barrels of petroleum products per day to about 90 countries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第三，贸易有好处。它可以提高经济效益，当我们从生产成本低于我们的地方购买东西时，我们就会受益。尽管你读不到这么多，但美国也是石油产品出口大国，每天向约 90 个国家出售约 200 万桶石油产品。

paragraphs.sourceText: There is no question that the United States imports a great deal of energy and, in fact, relies on that steady flow to maintain its economy. When that flow is interrupted, we feel the pain in short supplies and higher prices. At the same time, we derive massive economic benefits when we buy the most affordable energy on the world market and when we engage in energy trade around the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 毫无疑问，美国进口大量能源，事实上，美国依靠稳定的能源进口来维持其经济。当这种流动被中断时，我们就会感受到供应短缺和价格上涨的痛苦。与此同时，当我们购买世界市场上最便宜的能源并在世界各地进行能源贸易时，我们获得了巨大的经济利益。
